messages.content: Find out about traffic laws in Texas.

function.name: lawsuit_search
function.description: Search for lawsuits related to a particular subject matter in a certain location. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

location.description: The location to perform the search in.

subject.description: The subject matter of the lawsuits.

year.description: Optional. The year in which the lawsuit was filed. Default: 2024

message.content:
Here’s a concise overview of key Texas traffic laws (as of 2024). For detailed statutes, see the Texas Transportation Code and the Texas Department of Public Safety (DPS) website. | Topic | Key Points | Relevant Statutes / Resources | |-------|------------|------------------------------| | **Speed Limits** | • Posted limits apply unless otherwise indicated.
• Rural interstate highways: 70 mph (unless posted lower).
• Urban interstate highways: 65 mph.
• School zones: 25 mph during school hours; 35 mph after. | §545.001–545.004 (Texas Transportation Code); DPS Speed Limit Signs | | **Seat‑belt & Child‑seat Laws** | • All drivers and passengers must wear seat belts.
• Children under 8 must be in a child safety seat or booster.
• No “no‑seat‑belt” exemptions. | §545.021 (Seat‑belt law); §545.022 (Child‑seat law) | | **DUI / Alcohol** | • Blood alcohol concentration (BAC) ≥ 0.08 % is illegal for all drivers.
• Zero‑tolerance for drivers under 21 (BAC ≥ 0.02 %).
• Penalties include fines, license suspension, mandatory alcohol‑education programs, and possible jail time. | §545.041 (Impaired Driving); §545.042 (Zero‑Tolerance) | | **Texting & Phone Use** | • Drivers may not text, email, or use a phone without hands‑free equipment.
• Cell‑phone‑use restrictions also apply to pedestrians in crosswalks. | §545.051 (Cell‑Phone Use) | | **Right‑of‑Way & Intersection Rules** | • Yield to pedestrians at crosswalks.
• Stop at red lights and stop signs.
• Right‑of‑way rules for turns, merging, and emergency vehicles. | §545.011–545.014 (Traffic Control Devices) | | **School Bus Law** | • Vehicles must stop when a school bus stops with its stop sign extended and flashing red lights.
• Failure to stop can result in heavy penalties. | §545.015 (School Bus Law) | | **Lane‑Changing & Overtaking** | • Must signal before changing lanes.
• Overtaking on the right is prohibited unless passing a stopped vehicle. | §545.013 (Lane‑Changing) | | **Parking Regulations** | • Parking in front of driveways, fire hydrants, or on sidewalks is prohibited.
• No parking within 20 ft of a crosswalk. | §545.019 (Parking) | | **Vehicle Equipment Requirements** | • Headlights, taillights, brake lights, turn signals, and horn must be functional.
• Mirrors must be present and properly adjusted. | §545.020 (Equipment) | | **Insurance & Liability** | • Minimum liability coverage required: $30,000 bodily injury per person, $60,000 total bodily injury, $25,000 property damage.
• Proof of insurance must be carried. | §545.030 (Insurance) | | **Towing & Vehicle Removal** | • Towing of abandoned or unsafe vehicles requires a permit from local authorities.
• Violations can lead to fines and vehicle impoundment. | §545.025 (Vehicle Removal) | ### How to Find Specific Laws or Recent Changes 1. **Texas Transportation Code** – Available online at the Texas Legislature’s website. 2. **Texas DPS Traffic Law Handbook** – Updated annually; includes practical examples and enforcement guidelines. 3. **Local County Ordinances** – Some counties have additional speed limits or parking regulations. ### Common Enforcement Practices - **Speed Cameras** – Used in many urban areas; violations result in automatic tickets. - **Random Breath‑Testing** – Conducted by police officers; failure to comply can lead to arrest. - **Electronic Toll Collection** – E‑Tag usage is encouraged; toll violations are billed automatically. --- #### Quick Reference Links - [Texas DPS Traffic Law Handbook](https://www.dps.texas.gov/section/traffic-law-handbook) - [Texas Transportation Code (PDF)](https://statutes.capitol.texas.gov/) - [Texas Legislature Online – Transportation Code](https://capitol.texas.gov/codes/transportationcode.htm) Feel free to let me know if you’d like deeper details on any specific section or recent case law!
